target_architecture: One coherent logical database with compact shared authoritative state and selectively activated exact physical/execution experts. Make ordinary state implicit where useful, represent sparse deviations, and choose durable, reconstructable or ephemeral lifetimes by measured whole-system cost. Seek joint speed, CPU and memory improvements rather than separate full specialist copies.
architecture_integration_boundary: The native library exports spi storage and transactions. Factorization, certificates, shared arrangements and other research kernels are in the separate historical executable, not dispatched by the native comparison adapter. Explicit value-cache/grouped-update controls are not the research's automatic admission, routing or lifecycle controller. Shared logical correctness is partially implemented, but compact pages, implicit extent mapping, bounded sparse overlays, fine version reuse and resource-governed expert integration remain incomplete. SQLite losses describe this native baseline, not an integrated mixture-of-experts result. They remain real deficiencies to address.
next_integration: Attribute baseline costs using phase CPU, I/O calls/bytes, allocations and publication timing. Existing elapsed-time trials do not establish CPU or RSS improvements.
Integrate scan-friendly arbitrary-key pages, fixed-extent implicit mapping and bounded sparse updates under the same logical transaction and recovery API, retaining the AVL control.
Specify expert semantic eligibility, snapshot coverage, state lifetime and admission/retirement cost. Reject stale or incomplete expert coverage rather than filter only existing candidates.
Connect eligible research mechanisms through shared state with explicit typed query/update contracts where required. Do not infer arithmetic semantics from arbitrary binary values.

Measure full lifecycle resource vectors and no-expert fallback overhead, with predeclared tolerances, uncertainty and adversarial workload shifts. No universal superiority claim without matched specialist evidence.

value_cache_boundary: Disabled by default. Point reads alone admit values up to 4096 bytes and capacity-plus-metadata charge up to one eighth of the shared budget. Scans and compaction do not admit values. The committed-source trials support repeated-key reuse, not a general speedup. The reported 0.4-microsecond per-call median is below the lab's 1-microsecond reporting threshold and does not support a precise latency ratio. Unique reads and scans show no consistent benefit; 1 KiB-cache trials admit no values and show overhead. FIFO point admission may waste work or evict nodes under one-touch traffic. Cache charge and container capacities are not allocated-byte/RSS guarantees. No file format or durability barrier changes.
compaction_boundary: Preparation and data sync run outside the foreground state mutex. Publication still acquires it and syncs the manifest. Compaction and collection serialize through a maintenance lock. Any intervening commit invalidates the candidate, requiring explicit retry. No foreground latency bound, bounded retry cost, or bandwidth isolation is established.
grouped_update_boundary: Disabled by default. Empty-tree insert batches and replacement-only batches may share immutable ancestors. Deletes, mixed structural batches, single-key writes, oversized scratch batches and allocation failure use the proven sequential path. Temporary borrowed-entry references are capped at 64 KiB and one eighth of transaction_bytes, separately from staging charge. Bulk construction changes tree topology and serialized bytes. Replacement-only batches preserve topology, publication barriers and logical revisions. Correctness regressions and all 18 committed-source campaign trials passed. Median update-phase arena bytes fell 51% and total pre-maintenance arena bytes fell 14%. Normal-cache update time fell from 101.97 to 87.29 ms, and 1 KiB update time fell from 174.38 to 164.42 ms. Normal-cache load and single-row mutations were nearly unchanged, and ranges regressed slightly. SQLite remained faster. The result supports opt-in use only, not a general speedup or production-readiness claim. See results/spi/grouped-normal-committed-v1/summary.json and results/spi/grouped-small-committed-v1/summary.json. Arena counters exclude manifests and measure application-written bytes, not device write amplification.
benchmark_boundary: Same local binary-key operation stream is not equivalent full database semantics. Cache-cleared API calls are not device-cold reads. Single-row mutation tests must actually change the stored value. Keep old benchmark schemas as historical evidence only.
historical_lab: Existing kernel results and known ranking/numeric defects are separate from this new storage baseline. A passing lab test does not establish arbitrary-input correctness or validate this engine.
